paper.title_en: Lean-Verified Discovery of Exact Nonadditive Quantum Codes with Artificial Intelligence Assistants
paper.abstract_en: Exact scientific discovery requires more than heuristic search: Candidate constructions must be turned into exact objects and checked independently. We address this gap by extending TeXRA with an independent Lean 4 verification layer, turning it into a human-driven, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted discovery protocol with specialized Synthesis, Search, and Verification Agents for exact scientific discovery. The protocol combines symbolic synthesis, combinatorial and linear-programming search, exact reconstruction of numerical candidates, and formal verification. We apply it to nonadditive quantum error-correcting codes with prescribed transversal diagonal gates within the subset-sum linear-programming (SSLP) framework. In the distance-2 regime where logical states occupy distinct residue classes, the resulting Lean-certified catalog contains 14 116 codes for <math><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> and up to six physical qubits, realizing cyclic logical orders 2 through 18, from which we extract closed-form infinite families. We also construct a residue-degenerate ((6, 4, 2)) code implementing the logical controlled-phase gate <math><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. At distance 3, we resolve the transversal-<math><mi>T</mi></math> problem for ((7, 2, 3)) codes within the complementary binary-dihedral <math><msub><mi>BD</mi><mn>16</mn></msub></math> setting: Among the 12 candidates surviving the SSLP filters, 10 admit exact realizations and 2 are excluded by no-go proofs. All accepted constructions, families, and no-go results are formalized and checked in Lean, showing how AI-assisted workflows can bridge search, exact reconstruction, and formal proof in the physical sciences.
